newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Kirishi oil refiner on course for 97 target.
newsitem.headline: Russia Kirishi oil refiner on course for 97 target.

text.p: Russia's huge Kirishi oil refinery, strategically located in the northwest close to the European oil products trading hub of Rotterdam, is on course to meet its 1997 output targets, a plant official said on Thursday.

Grigory Zalishchevsky, a technical director, said Kirishinefteorgsintez (KINEF) would process around 16.0 million tonnes (320,000 barrels per day) of crude oil in 1997, against 15.3 million (306,000 bpd) in 1996.
"We are still expecting to meet our overall processing target this year of around 16 million tonnes," he said.
Nikolai Laptev, the refinery's financial director, said in May the official throughput target this year was 16.2 million tonnes. The refinery was Russia's third biggest by output last year.
Zalishchevsky said there would be no major changes in the mix of products produced at the plant.

"So far this year, we are producing according to our plans," he said by telephone from the plant. "There have been no reductions in crude supplies, and there will not be any major changes in the amount of each product we produce."
He said that trying to squeeze out more light products meeting European quality standards without a costly new hydro-cracking unit would not be possible.
"If we succeed in producing slightly more light products, then output of heavy fuel oil could slip but it would not be by much," he said.

KINEF is a key supplier of heavy fuel oil to Western markets. Fuel oil is by far the refinery's single biggest product, with output last year at 4.95 million tonnes and a further 0.83 million tonnes of bunker fuel.
KINEF expects to receive regular crude supplies this year from Surgutneftegaz, the production arm of KINEF's owner Surgut Holding (NK Surgutneftegaz), Zalishchevsky said.
The refinery relies mainly on Surgutneftegaz crude but also buys top-up volumes through trading companies.
Surgutneftegaz is building a $200 million oil terminal in the Gulf of Finland which will be able to handle 15 million tonnes of heavy fuel oil and gasoline annually.
A pipeline costing another $100 million will also be built connecting KINEF with the terminal.
